decode_layout: Exactly 160 bytes required; if input.len() < 160 the harness returns an EMPTY Vec (total decode, no panic). All values little-endian. offset 0..32 = z: [u64;4] (scalar-field element mod n); 32..64 = r: [u64;4]; 64..96 = s: [u64;4]; 96..160 = q: [u64;8] = Qx[u64;4] || Qy[u64;4] (base-field elements mod p). Each [u64;N] is N consecutive LE u64s, limb i at bytes [8*i, 8*i+8) of that field, so the whole block is the limb arrays concatenated in LE order. Bytes past offset 160 are ignored. OUTPUT: exactly 2 bytes — byte0 = stage (0x00 signature VALID, 0x01 ecdsa_verify returned Err, 0x02 z non-canonical Fr, 0x03 r non-canonical Fr, 0x04 s non-canonical Fr, 0x05 q invalid point/non-canonical Fq); byte1 = P256Error code (0 when stage 0x00; 1 InvalidFqElement, 2 InvalidFrElement, 3 NotOnCurve, 4 QAtInfinity, 5 ROrSZero, 6 RxMismatch, 7 InvalidGlvSignWord). A known-good RFC-6979 P-256 seed vector is embedded verbatim in the DECODE comment for the input generator; mutating any limb of z/r/s still drives the full Fake-GLV path and reports RxMismatch rather than panicking.
entry_called: jolt_inlines_p256::ecdsa_verify(z, r, s, q), preceded by P256Fr::from_u64_arr for z/r/s and P256Point::from_u64_arr for q, all wrapped in the #[inline(never)] shim run_p256_ecdsa_verify so the symbol survives lto=fat for --trace-fn
